title: Grade 5 French — Mon, Jun 23
description: Les métiers — Day 1 of 5: Common professions vocabulary
subject: french

questions.question: What does 'un médecin' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Un médecin' = a doctor. 'Il est médecin.' = He is a doctor. Note: professions often drop the article after être: 'Il est médecin' (not 'Il est un médecin' in formal usage).

questions.question: What is 'un professeur'?
questions.explanation: 'Un professeur' = a professor/teacher. Can also be shortened to 'un prof' (informal). 'Elle est professeur de mathématiques.'

questions.question: What does 'un cuisinier' do?
options: cooks food — is a cook or chef
questions.explanation: 'Un cuisinier' = a cook (male). From 'cuisine' (kitchen/cooking). 'Il est cuisinier dans un restaurant.' = He is a cook in a restaurant.

questions.question: What is 'un ingénieur'?
questions.explanation: 'Un ingénieur' = an engineer. Note the accent: 'ingénieur' (é). 'Elle est ingénieure en informatique.' = She is a software engineer.

questions.question: What does 'un policier' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Un policier' = a police officer. From 'police.' 'Le policier arrête le voleur.' = The police officer arrests the thief.

questions.question: What is 'un acteur'?
questions.explanation: 'Un acteur' = an actor (male). From Latin 'actor.' 'Il est acteur de cinéma.' = He is a film actor.

questions.question: Translate: 'He is a singer.'
questions.explanation: 'Il est chanteur.' = He is a singer. 'Chanteur' = singer (male). From 'chanter' (to sing).

questions.question: What does 'un agriculteur' do?
options: farms the land — is a farmer
questions.explanation: 'Un agriculteur' = a farmer. From 'agriculture.' 'L'agriculteur cultive la terre.' = The farmer cultivates the land. 'Agriculture' = farming.

questions.question: What is 'un pompier'?
questions.explanation: 'Un pompier' = a firefighter. 'Les pompiers éteignent le feu.' = The firefighters put out the fire.

questions.question: What profession describes someone who flies airplanes?
questions.explanation: 'Un pilote' = a pilot. 'Il est pilote de ligne.' = He is an airline pilot. 'Pilote' is also used for race car drivers ('pilote de formule 1').

questions.question: In French, professions after 'être' often drop the article. Which is CORRECT?
options: Both are acceptable in all contexts.
questions.explanation: Both are used: 'Il est médecin' (formal/literary, no article — classic French rule) and 'Il est un médecin' (more colloquial, especially when adding an adjective: 'Il est un bon médecin'). Both are grammatically acceptable.

questions.question: What does 'un architecte' do?
questions.explanation: 'Un architecte' = an architect — designs buildings, plans structures. 'L'architecte dessine les plans.' = The architect draws the plans.

questions.question: 'Je veux devenir médecin.' means:
options: I want to become a doctor.
I don't want to be a doctor.
questions.explanation: 'Je veux devenir médecin.' = I want to become a doctor. 'Veux' = want (from 'vouloir'). 'Devenir' = to become.

questions.question: Match profession to description: 'Il soigne les animaux malades.'
questions.explanation: 'Il soigne les animaux malades.' = He treats sick animals. 'Un vétérinaire' = a vet. 'Soigner' = to treat/care for.

questions.question: Why do many French profession names end in '-eur' (chanteur, acteur, ingénieur)?
options: The '-eur' suffix comes from Latin '-or/-ator' and indicates a person who performs an action (chanter→chanteur: one who sings; agir→acteur: one who acts)
It is an informal suffix only
questions.explanation: The '-eur' suffix marks 'agent' — one who does something. Latin origin: '-or/-ator.' English equivalents: '-or/-er' (actor, singer, engineer). This suffix helps recognise new profession words even without knowing them.
